card.name: Space before flags after ls command
card.fires_on: The space and dash that follow the shell command "ls" just before a flag like -l, -le or -Z. It also fires on the "aux" after "ps" in Unix examples.

modes.label: Flags after ls
modes.description: The dash or space token right after "ls" in a terminal example, before the option letters.
modes.example: file You can use the new "-e" option to the "ls" command to show a file's ACL from the command line. % ls<< ->>le file -rw------- 1 john

modes.label: ps options
modes.description: The option word after "ps" in a command line, before a trailing Z flag.
modes.example: something else. # setenforce 0 To view the contexts that a process is running with, add the Z option to ps: # ps<< aux>>Z | grep httpd system_u

modes.label: Glasgow place lists
modes.description: Commas or "in" inside a list of Scottish towns near Glasgow, a weaker and unrelated case.
modes.example: In the 1910s and 1920s the urban sprawl around Glasgow, including the towns Clydebank<<,>> Greenock, and Paisley were centres

card.plain: It marks the spot in a Unix command where option flags such as -l or -Z come next after ls.
